Quantizing only the 11.7M-parameter embedding table gives max delta 0.0094 and saves 34 MiB, so the embedding is not where agreement is lost; the 10.6M encoder-layer weights are.

claim: AGAINST OUR INTEREST: the single best held-out number this project has ever produced was discarded, because its positive control failed a floor fixed before it was measured.
proof: cross-encoder/nli-MiniLM2-L6-H768 scores macro held-out 0.896 - higher than the selected scorer's 0.880 - on a positive control of 0.684, below the 0.75 floor. A control under the floor means the scorer cannot tell two DIFFERENT dimensions apart, so its pole separation is not evidence about the dimension it is credited to. All four were excluded and none of their numbers was used.
method: POSITIVE_CONTROL_FLOOR = 0.75 was fixed in export/encoder_ablation.py during increment 3, before any increment-4 variant existed, and is imported rather than restated. That is the only reason it can be applied to a 0.896 without being an excuse. Stated plainly: this is a finding that these scorers' numbers are UNREADABLE under this protocol, not a finding that cross-encoders are worse - a protocol able to read them was not built.
